title: ADscan technical report v2
description: technical_report.json: every finding, positive control and event a scan recorded, per domain, plus the report-time blocks the deliverables and the web platform read instead of recomputing (exposure score, KPIs, compliance, coverage statements). Written by one writer (adscan_core/reporting/technical_report.py). Version marker: schema_version, '2.<minor>'. A minor bump adds optional fields or blocks; a reader of any 2.x accepts every 2.x file. Objects that list their properties are declared: within a major an engine may add fields to them, so do not reject unknown keys. Objects without properties (details, evidence entries, knowledge, the per-domain report blocks) are opaque: their content is not frozen by this contract, and the blocks that carry their own schema_version (exposure_kpis, compliance, ...) version themselves. No recovered password, hash or key value is ever written into this file.

coverage_run_id.$comment: Id of the recorded run that last wrote the file; coverage.json is trusted for this file only when its run_id matches.

licence.$comment: Since 2.5. Present only when the run was made under a PRO licence: the identifiers the licence server issued (grant, licence document, installation), so a report traces back to the grant that produced it. Never a secret.

domains.$comment: Keyed by domain FQDN (lower case). A domain is listed as soon as any producer names it; assessment.enumerated says whether it was actually enumerated.

asset_scope.$comment: Since 2.9. Present when the run had an asset scope: the scope revision and digest it ended under (scope.json asset_scope), who decided it and when, and the run-wide counts. Per-domain detail is in domains.<d>.asset_scope_coverage.

environment_changes.$comment: Copy of the change ledger attached at session end ({summary, changes}); environment_changes.json is the authoritative file.

compliance_decision.$comment: Added in 2.3. The compliance-framework answer the last scan or render ran with: decision 'frameworks' lists the selected framework keys; decision 'none' means the assessor decided no compliance framework applies to the organisation, so the report carries no compliance mapping. Absent means no decision was recorded (nothing was chosen), never 'none applies'.

asset_scope_item.$comment: Since 2.7. One object the asset scope kept out of the assessment. entry_written_as is how the deciding scope entry was written and known_as how the target was known, so an address entry that matched a host reached by name is stated in both forms.

assessment.$comment: Whether the domain was enumerated (record_domain_assessment) and, since 2.11, whether the assessment finished (record_assessment_integrity). complete is false and incomplete_phases names each phase that ran but did not finish its work (a domain controller that stopped answering, a lost collection connection, a memory stop, an operator stop); both are absent when no phase was recorded incomplete, which is not by itself a claim that every check ran. A reason starting target_unreachable means the phase's domain controller stopped answering and its checks were not evaluated.

asset_scope_coverage.$comment: Since 2.9. Present when the run had an asset scope (an allow or deny list of hosts and directory objects, scope.json asset_scope). Built by adscan_core/reporting/engagement_scope.py build_asset_scope_coverage. excluded lists the objects of this domain the scope kept out of the assessment (at most 200; excluded_omitted counts the rest), each with how it was identified; the counts are exact. directory_only_dcs are domain controllers used for directory reads only. routes_not_executed and steps_not_executed are null until the scan counted them. statement is the sentence the report prints. An excluded object was never contacted or acted on: it is never a finding and never clean.

excluded.$comment: Population 1: objects the client excluded, or did not list on an allow list (reason denied_entry or not_in_allow_list).

unconfirmed.$comment: Population 2, never merged with the first: objects ADscan could not confirm as within the scope and left alone as a precaution (reason identity_undetermined or scope_record_unreadable). cause says what was missing: name_not_resolved, address_not_attributed, entry_not_matched, affected_hosts_unknown, scope_record_unreadable or unknown.

entry_outcomes.$comment: Since 2.10. What became of each scope entry the client wrote, for this domain: entries (at most 200, the ones needing attention first; omitted counts the rest), counts by outcome, and deny_matched_nothing. outcome is one of matched, matched_assessed, matched_excluded, matched_not_reached, matched_not_confirmed, matched_nothing. An entry tied to no domain (an address no computer holds, a name that matched nothing) is listed under every domain.

guest_access_coverage.$comment: Since 2.8. Hosts guest SMB access was never asked of, because the guest name's absence from the directory could not be confirmed and guest probing stopped after a few refusals (adscan_core/reporting/guest_access_coverage.py). Absent when every host was asked.

resource_coverage.$comment: Since 2.6. Every pipeline stage that stopped at the memory ceiling for this domain (adscan_core/reporting/resource_coverage.py): stage is collection, graph_build, graph_export, attack_paths, report or unknown (no stage was running); examined and total count the stage's unit; statement is the sentence the report prints. Absent when every stage finished. Since 2.12 a stage may also be mssql_post_auth (the work on a database server after sign-in) or mssql_file_review (the file listing on a database server), and reason may be listing_limit: the listing stopped at its fixed bound, with examined the files listed. Since 2.13 a stage may also be winrm_post_auth (the file search on a host over Windows Remote Management after sign-in) or winrm_file_review (the file listing on such a host, which stops at a fixed bound the same way), share_mapping (the file review of network shares, counted in shares, stopped for memory) or share_file_listing (shares whose file listing was cut short: examined counts the shares listed whole, total every share listed), and reason may also be listing_incomplete: a listing ran out of its time budget or ended on an error.

examined.$comment: null when the stage's progress is unknown (the memory sentinel stopped a stage that does not count its units).

run_id.$comment: Since 2.7. The run that recorded the stop: the same run does not retry a stopped graph build, a later run does and clears the stop on success.

operator_stop_coverage.$comment: Since 2.4. {stops: [{action, step_id, label, phase_id, phase_title, examined, total, unit, source, statement}]}: every step the operator stopped, phase skipped or scan stopped early, with the client statement (adscan_core/reporting/operator_stop_coverage.py). Absent when nothing was stopped.

scan_policy_coverage.$comment: Self-versioned block (adscan_core/scan_policy/coverage.py). Since 2.2 it may carry agreed_policy: {name, revision, digest, matches, reason?}, the policy agreed with the client for the engagement and whether this run's digest matches it; absent when none was agreed.

finding.$comment: One weakness per key and domain. severity is the authored baseline band; adscan_severity is ADscan's contextual rating of this instance and the one a report counts.

alias_keys.$comment: Present only on a merged finding: the keys of every producer that recorded the same weakness (an alias family), in document order. The finding carries the family's canonical key.

cvss_base.$comment: Present only together with cvss_base_vector, which reproduces it.

control_evidence.$comment: A positive or neutral observation (a control verified in place, a check that ran and found the weakness absent). Never a finding.
